title: Uterine Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for uterine / endometrial cancer. Entry by newly-diagnosed vs advanced / recurrent, then histology (endometrioid, serous / clear-cell, carcinosarcoma, uterine sarcoma / LMS), molecular class (POLE / MMRd / p53abn / NSMP), primary surgery (with a fertility-sparing response-adapted branch), risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, response / restaging after definitive locoregional therapy, then surveillance and a biomarker-directed advanced pathway with explicit line-of-therapy progression sub-trees (first line -> on progression -> later line) for each molecular / receptor subgroup and for advanced leiomyosarcoma. Each treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id where one fits; agents and surgery / radiation without a matching dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup / staging / subtype-stratification content is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text; structural pathway consistent with standard references (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison). Invents no dose / regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses. FollowCare rules never alter these orders.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN, DeVita, Harrison). Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Molecular classification (POLE, mismatch-repair / MSI, p53) is recommended on all endometrial carcinomas; it refines prognosis and adjuvant intensity independent of grade and stage.

b.text: POLE ultramutated tumors have an excellent prognosis; de-escalation or omission of adjuvant therapy in early stage may be considered case-by-case, ideally within a trial.

c.text: Vaginal brachytherapy alone gives fewer bowel and bladder effects than external-beam pelvic RT and controls the vaginal cuff well in high-intermediate-risk early-stage endometrioid disease.

d.text: Add an immune-checkpoint inhibitor to carboplatin / paclitaxel for advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma; benefit is largest in MMR-deficient / MSI-high tumors.

e.text: After progression on platinum in mismatch-repair-proficient disease, lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab improves survival versus chemotherapy; monitor for hypertension, proteinuria, and fatigue.

f.text: For leiomyosarcoma avoid tumor morcellation; anthracycline-based therapy is a standard first-line option and gemcitabine / docetaxel an accepted alternative, with non-cross-resistant agents on later progression.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Uterine cancer - initial evaluation
nodes.description: Confirm tissue diagnosis and complete baseline staging workup before choosing a pathway.
bullets: History, exam including pelvic exam, performance status
Endometrial biopsy or D&C with expert gyn-pathology review; record histology and grade
CBC, chemistries, LFTs; consider CA-125 in high-risk histology
Imaging: pelvic MRI for local extent; CT chest / abdomen / pelvis or PET for suspected advanced disease

bullets.label: Molecular / IHC panel
bullets.sub: MMR / MSI, p53, and POLE where available; ER / PR and HER2 on serous or advanced disease

bullets: Assess surgical candidacy and fertility-sparing wishes

nodes.name: Disease scope
nodes.title: Newly diagnosed vs advanced / recurrent
nodes.description: Choose the clinical scenario that fits the patient now.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Uterine histology
nodes.description: Management branches first by tumor type. Choose the applicable histology.
bullets: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma (type I)
Serous or clear-cell carcinoma (high-risk type II)
Carcinosarcoma (dedifferentiated / MMMT)
Uterine sarcoma including leiomyosarcoma (LMS)

nodes.name: Molecular class
nodes.title: Endometrioid - molecular classification
nodes.description: Assign one of four molecular subgroups; it modifies prognosis and adjuvant intensity.

tables.title: Molecular subgroups of endometrial carcinoma
rows: Consider de-escalation / omit in early stage
Loss of MLH1 / PMS2 / MSH2 / MSH6
Standard by stage; IO candidate if advanced

nodes.name: Primary therapy (EC)
nodes.title: Primary therapy - endometrioid
nodes.description: Standard is hysterectomy with surgical staging; a fertility-sparing progestin approach is an option only in highly selected grade-1 IA disease.
bullets: Total hysterectomy + BSO (minimally invasive preferred when feasible)
Sentinel-lymph-node mapping for nodal assessment; full lymphadenectomy selectively
Peritoneal assessment and cytology; omental / peritoneal biopsies if serous features
Fertility-sparing progestin only in highly selected grade-1 IA disease with counseling and close follow-up

nodes.name: Fertility-sparing response
nodes.title: Fertility-sparing progestin - response assessment
nodes.description: Re-biopsy at 3-6 months determines whether conservative therapy continues or definitive surgery is needed.
bullets: Continuous progestin (oral or levonorgestrel IUD); endometrial sampling every 3-6 months
Complete response: attempt conception promptly; maintain surveillance sampling
Definitive hysterectomy after childbearing or for persistent / progressive disease

nodes.name: Stage / risk
nodes.title: Post-surgical stage and risk group
nodes.description: Combine FIGO stage, grade, LVSI, and molecular class into a risk group to select adjuvant therapy.

tables.title: Simplified FIGO stage groups (endometrial)
rows: Confined to corpus (IA no / less-than-half myometrium; IB half or more)
Cervical stromal invasion, no extrauterine spread
Local / regional spread (serosa, adnexa, vagina, pelvic / para-aortic nodes)
Bladder / bowel mucosa (IVA) or distant metastases (IVB)

options.label: Stage I high-intermediate risk (IB, grade 3, or LVSI)

nodes.name: Low-risk observation
nodes.title: Stage I low-risk - observation
nodes.description: Excellent prognosis; no adjuvant therapy after complete surgery, proceed to surveillance.
bullets: No adjuvant radiation or chemotherapy for stage IA grade 1-2 endometrioid
POLE-ultramutated tumors reinforce a de-escalation / observation choice
Vaginal brachytherapy only if isolated adverse features emerge on review
Then surveillance

nodes.name: HIR adjuvant
nodes.title: High-intermediate-risk adjuvant choice
nodes.description: Choose adjuvant radiation modality; molecular class informs de-escalation.

options.label: External-beam pelvic RT (extensive LVSI / node concern)

nodes.name: VBT
nodes.title: Vaginal brachytherapy
nodes.description: Vaginal cuff brachytherapy to reduce local recurrence with low toxicity.
bullets: Vaginal-cuff brachytherapy over 3-5 fractions
No cytotoxic chemotherapy for isolated HIR endometrioid
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Pelvic EBRT
nodes.title: External-beam pelvic radiotherapy
nodes.description: External-beam pelvic RT for substantial LVSI or nodal-risk early-stage disease.
bullets: External-beam pelvic RT +/- vaginal-brachytherapy boost
Add carboplatin / paclitaxel only if p53-abnormal or upstaged
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Stage II adjuvant
nodes.title: Stage II - adjuvant radiation +/- chemotherapy
nodes.description: Cervical stromal invasion warrants pelvic RT; add chemotherapy for grade-3 or p53-abnormal tumors.
bullets: External-beam pelvic RT with vaginal-brachytherapy boost
Add carboplatin / paclitaxel for grade-3, LVSI-heavy, or p53-abnormal disease
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Stage III-IVA definitive
nodes.title: Locoregional advanced - chemotherapy + radiation
nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy is the backbone for stage III-IVA, with directed RT for local control; then restage.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel systemic chemotherapy
Add an immune-checkpoint inhibitor, benefit greatest if MMRd / MSI-high
Tumor-directed / pelvic RT for local control as indicated
Then restage to decide surveillance vs continued systemic therapy

nodes.name: Locoregional response
nodes.title: Response after definitive locoregional therapy
nodes.description: Restaging after chemoradiation determines whether the patient enters surveillance or moves to advanced systemic therapy.

options.label: Residual or progressive disease - systemic therapy

nodes.name: Surgery (high-risk)
nodes.title: Primary surgery - serous / clear-cell / carcinosarcoma
nodes.description: Comprehensive surgical staging as for ovarian cancer; these histologies spread early.
bullets: Total hysterectomy + BSO with comprehensive staging
Omentectomy, peritoneal biopsies, and washings (serous behaves like ovarian)
Sentinel-node / nodal assessment
Maximal cytoreduction if visible extrauterine disease

nodes.name: High-risk stage
nodes.title: High-risk histology - stage group
nodes.description: Even early-stage serous / clear-cell / carcinosarcoma usually receives systemic therapy.

nodes.name: Early high-risk
nodes.title: Stage I high-risk histology - chemotherapy + brachytherapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant chemotherapy plus vaginal brachytherapy given the high relapse risk of these subtypes.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel adjuvant chemotherapy
Vaginal brachytherapy for cuff control
Add trastuzumab for HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma
Then surveillance

nodes.name: Advanced high-risk
nodes.title: Stage II-IVA high-risk histology - chemotherapy +/- RT
nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy backbone with directed RT; biomarker add-ons where positive, then restage.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel chemotherapy
Add trastuzumab if HER2-positive serous; add checkpoint inhibitor if MMRd
Tumor-directed RT for local control
Then restage to decide surveillance vs continued systemic therapy

nodes.name: High-risk response
nodes.title: Response after primary systemic therapy - high-risk histology
nodes.description: Restaging determines surveillance versus transition to biomarker-directed advanced therapy.

nodes.name: Sarcoma subtype
nodes.title: Uterine sarcoma subtype
nodes.description: Sarcoma management diverges sharply by subtype; confirm on expert pathology.

nodes.name: LMS extent
nodes.title: Leiomyosarcoma - disease extent
nodes.description: LMS is managed by resectability; surgery is the mainstay for localized disease.

nodes.name: Localized LMS
nodes.title: Localized LMS - surgery then observation
nodes.description: Complete resection (avoid morcellation) with observation; adjuvant therapy is not standard.
bullets: Total hysterectomy without morcellation; BSO individualized
No routine adjuvant chemotherapy or RT for uterus-limited disease
Consider adjuvant therapy or a trial for high-risk cases after discussion
Then close surveillance including chest imaging

nodes.name: LMS systemic
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - start systemic therapy
nodes.description: Begin first-line systemic therapy for advanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma; consider metastasectomy for isolated disease.

nodes.name: LMS first line
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - first-line chemotherapy
nodes.description: Doxorubicin-based or gemcitabine / docetaxel combinations are standard first-line options.
bullets: Doxorubicin single-agent or anthracycline-based combination
Gemcitabine / docetaxel is an accepted alternative first-line doublet
Assess response by imaging every 2-3 cycles
On progression, move to a non-cross-resistant later line

nodes.name: LMS 1L outcome
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - outcome on first line
nodes.description: Continue first-line therapy while it controls disease; switch on progression.

nodes.name: LMS second line
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - second-line therapy
nodes.description: Switch to a non-cross-resistant regimen after first-line progression.
bullets: Gemcitabine / docetaxel if an anthracycline was used first-line (or the reverse)
Consider trabectedin or pazopanib as active single agents
Reassess response; on further progression move to a later line or trial

nodes.name: LMS 2L outcome
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - outcome on second line
nodes.description: Continue while controlled; on further progression move to later-line single agents or a trial.

nodes.name: LMS later line
nodes.title: Advanced LMS - later-line therapy
nodes.description: Non-cross-resistant single agents after progression; trials encouraged.
bullets: Other active single agents: trabectedin, pazopanib, dacarbazine, eribulin
Clinical trial strongly encouraged
Best supportive care and symptom-directed palliation as appropriate

nodes.name: Low-grade ESS
nodes.title: Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma
nodes.description: Hormonally driven; surgery plus endocrine therapy, avoid estrogen.
bullets: Total hysterectomy + BSO (oophorectomy given hormone sensitivity)
Adjuvant or palliative endocrine therapy: aromatase inhibitor or progestin
Avoid estrogen replacement
Then surveillance

nodes.name: High-grade sarcoma
nodes.title: High-grade / undifferentiated uterine sarcoma
nodes.description: Aggressive; resection when feasible plus systemic chemotherapy, mirroring LMS systemic options.
bullets: Resection if operable; multidisciplinary sarcoma review
Systemic anthracycline- or gemcitabine-based chemotherapy for advanced disease
Test high-grade ESS for hormone receptors; targeted options if fusion-defined
Strong consideration for clinical trial, then surveillance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Structured follow-up; branch on whether recurrence is detected.
bullets: Symptom review and exam every 3-6 months for 2-3 years, then 6-12 monthly
Vaginal cuff / pelvic exam each visit; educate on bleeding or new symptoms
Imaging driven by symptoms or exam; chest imaging for sarcoma
No routine cytology or CA-125 unless clinically indicated

nodes.name: No recurrence
nodes.title: No evidence of disease - continue surveillance
nodes.description: Maintain the surveillance schedule and survivorship care.
bullets: Continue scheduled visits; de-escalate frequency over time
Address survivorship: bone health, sexual health, lifestyle, genetics
Refer for Lynch-syndrome genetic evaluation if MMRd / MSI-high

nodes.name: Recurrence site
nodes.title: Advanced / recurrent - site of disease
nodes.description: Isolated local recurrence may be salvaged with local therapy; disseminated disease needs systemic therapy.

nodes.name: Local salvage
nodes.title: Isolated local recurrence - salvage therapy
nodes.description: Curative-intent local therapy for an isolated recurrence, choice guided by prior radiation.
bullets: RT-naive vaginal recurrence: external-beam RT + brachytherapy (curative intent)
Prior pelvic RT: surgical resection / exenteration in selected patients
Restage to exclude occult distant disease first
Add systemic therapy by biomarker if disease is not truly isolated

nodes.name: Regional salvage
nodes.title: Regional nodal recurrence - directed therapy
nodes.description: Isolated nodal recurrence treated with directed local therapy plus systemic therapy.
bullets: External-beam RT to the involved nodal basin if not previously irradiated
Surgical resection of resectable nodal disease in selected patients
Add biomarker-directed systemic therapy for control of micrometastatic disease
Restage to exclude distant spread

nodes.name: Advanced biomarker
nodes.title: Metastatic carcinoma - biomarker-directed systemic therapy
nodes.description: Select the first-line systemic approach by MMR status, HER2, and hormone-receptor / grade; each arm then has an on-progression sub-tree.

nodes.name: MMRd first line
nodes.title: Metastatic MMRd - first-line chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: MMR-deficient tumors are highly immunotherapy-responsive; combine with the chemo backbone up front.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel plus a checkpoint inhibitor (dostarlimab or pembrolizumab)
Continue checkpoint-inhibitor maintenance per regimen after chemotherapy completion
Assess response by imaging every 2-3 cycles
On progression, move to single-agent immunotherapy or later options

nodes.name: MMRd 1L outcome
nodes.title: Metastatic MMRd - outcome on first line
nodes.description: Continue immunotherapy maintenance while it controls disease; switch on progression.

nodes.name: MMRd later line
nodes.title: Metastatic MMRd - later-line therapy
nodes.description: Later-line options after progression on chemo-immunotherapy.
bullets: Single-agent checkpoint inhibitor if not continued as maintenance
Sequential single-agent chemotherapy for immunotherapy-refractory disease
Consider a clinical trial; best supportive care as appropriate

nodes.name: pMMR first line
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR - first-line chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Chemotherapy plus checkpoint inhibitor is now first line for mismatch-repair-proficient advanced disease.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel plus a checkpoint inhibitor, then maintenance
Assess response by imaging every 2-3 cycles
On progression after platinum, move to lenvatinib + pembrolizumab

nodes.name: pMMR 1L outcome
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR - outcome on first line
nodes.description: Continue maintenance while controlled; switch to the lenvatinib + pembrolizumab doublet on progression.

nodes.name: pMMR second line
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR - lenvatinib + pembrolizumab
nodes.description: After platinum progression, lenvatinib + pembrolizumab improves survival versus chemotherapy.
bullets: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab after progression on platinum
Monitor and manage TKI toxicity (hypertension, proteinuria, fatigue); dose-modify as needed
Assess response by imaging; on further progression move to chemotherapy / ADC

nodes.name: pMMR 2L outcome
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR - outcome on second line
nodes.description: Continue the doublet while controlled; on further progression move to later-line therapy.

nodes.name: pMMR later line
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR - later-line therapy
nodes.description: Sequential single agents and antibody-drug conjugates after the lenvatinib + pembrolizumab doublet.
bullets: Sequential single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. doxorubicin, weekly paclitaxel)
Antibody-drug conjugate where biomarker-matched (guidance where no dose protocol exists here)
Clinical trial strongly encouraged; best supportive care as appropriate

nodes.name: HER2+ first line
nodes.title: HER2-positive serous - first-line chemo + HER2 therapy
nodes.description: Add HER2-directed therapy to the chemotherapy backbone for HER2-positive uterine serous carcinoma.
bullets: Carboplatin / paclitaxel + trastuzumab (HER2-positive serous)
Confirm HER2 status by validated IHC / ISH before starting
Assess response by imaging; on progression move to a HER2 antibody-drug conjugate

nodes.name: HER2+ 1L outcome
nodes.title: HER2-positive serous - outcome on first line
nodes.description: Continue while controlled; switch to a HER2 antibody-drug conjugate on progression.

nodes.name: HER2+ later line
nodes.title: HER2-positive serous - HER2 antibody-drug conjugate
nodes.description: Trastuzumab deruxtecan and other HER2-directed options after first-line progression.
bullets: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) after progression on chemo + trastuzumab
Monitor for interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis on the ADC
Sequential single-agent chemotherapy or trial on further progression

nodes.name: HR+ endocrine first line
nodes.title: Low-grade ER / PR-positive - first-line endocrine therapy
nodes.description: Endocrine therapy for indolent, low-volume, hormone-receptor-positive recurrent disease.
bullets: Progestin, aromatase inhibitor, or tamoxifen for ER / PR-positive low-grade disease
Reserve for low-volume, slow-growing, asymptomatic disease
On progression, intensify endocrine therapy or move to chemotherapy

nodes.name: HR+ 1L outcome
nodes.title: Low-grade ER / PR-positive - outcome on endocrine therapy
nodes.description: Continue endocrine therapy while it controls disease; intensify or switch on progression or symptomatic bulk.

nodes.name: HR+ later line
nodes.title: Low-grade ER / PR-positive - later-line therapy
nodes.description: Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor to endocrine therapy or switch to cytotoxic chemotherapy on progression.
bullets: Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor to an aromatase inhibitor where appropriate
Switch to carboplatin / paclitaxel chemotherapy for rapid progression or symptomatic bulk
Reassess biomarkers; consider a clinical trial
